content:
Class 5 fractions bring all four operations — including unlike denominators and division by fractions. This is one of the highest-weight Olympiad chapters. Here is what it tests, the rules, the traps, and a free 10-question test.

What the Class 5 Maths Olympiad Fractions chapter tests

  • Add/subtract with unlike denominators (LCM method)
  • Multiply and divide fractions (reciprocals)
  • Mixed ↔ improper conversions and simplest form
  • Comparing, ordering and fraction word problems

Key facts your child should know

  • Common denominator = LCM: 1/2 + 1/3 = 5/6.
  • Dividing = multiplying by the reciprocal: 3/4 ÷ 2/5 = 15/8.
  • Simplest form: divide both by the HCF.
  • 3/5 of 40 = 24 — divide by the bottom, times the top.

Common mistakes to avoid

  • Adding tops and bottoms straight across.
  • Forgetting to flip the second fraction when dividing.
  • Leaving answers unsimplified when simplest form is asked.

quiz.title: IMO Class 5 Fractions Quiz
quiz.intro: Ten Olympiad-pattern questions. Pick an answer for each, then press Check my score.

questions.explanation: Cross-multiply: 5 × 9 = 45 and 7 × 6 = 42. Since 45 > 42, 5/6 > 7/9, so the greater fraction is 5/6.

questions.q: Find the product of 5/12 and 8/15. (Give the answer in simplest form.)
questions.explanation: (5 × 8)/(12 × 15) = 40/180. Cancel the common factor 20 to get 2/9. In simplest form this is 2/9.

questions.q: Riya had Rs 240. She spent 1/3 of it on a book and then 1/4 of the remaining money on a pen. How much money is left with her?
questions.explanation: First step: 1/3 of 240 is used, so 240 − 80 = 160 remain. Second step: 1/4 of 160 = 40 is used, leaving 160 − 40 = 120.
Convert to improper fractions: 2 3/4 = 11/4 and 1 5/6 = 11/6. LCM of 4 and 6 is 12, so the sum is 33/12 + 22/12 = 55/12 = 4 7/12.
The missing fraction = 3/5 − 1/4. LCM of 5 and 4 is 20: 12/20 − 5/20 = 7/20 = 7/20.

questions.q: What fraction should be written in the box: [ ] + 2/5 = 9/10?

questions.explanation: The HCF of 45 and 60 is 15. Dividing both terms by 15: 45/60 = 3/4.

questions.q: Find the product of 7/10 and 5/14. (Give the answer in simplest form.)
questions.explanation: (7 × 5)/(10 × 14) = 35/140. Cancel the common factor 35 to get 1/4. In simplest form this is 1/4.

faq.q: How do you add fractions with different denominators?
faq.a: Rewrite both over their LCM, then add the numerators: 1/2 + 1/3 = 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.
The fraction flipped over — the reciprocal of 2/5 is 5/2. Dividing by a fraction means multiplying by its reciprocal.
